verdict.rationale: Fivetran ships an official MCP server that lets an agent check sync status and spot broken connections. Write operations can be unlocked via FIVETRAN_SCOPE, and the REST API supports programmatic management, but neither source explicitly documents triggering a sync or re-sync. Detecting broken connections is documented, but deeper diagnosis of why a run failed is not. Missing for 10: an explicitly documented API/MCP sync or re-sync trigger, documented failure-diagnosis detail such as error logs or causes, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can check sync status, diagnose a failed run, and re-trigger it through an API or MCP server

citations.quote: It allows you to ask read-only questions like "when was the last time my postgres connection completed a sync?" and "are any of my connections broken?"
Set `FIVETRAN_SCOPE` to `read/write` or `read/write/delete` to unlock write and delete operations
official MCP server documented at https://github.com/fivetran/fivetran-mcp
Set up and scale your data pipeline, and manage your Fivetran account programmatically using the Fivetran REST API.
